name: Start your online business
about: For first-time sellers in Nigeria. Learn what you need to start, how to choose who you sell to, test your idea before you spend, write product listings that sell, set simple shop rules and win your first ten customers.
for: New sellers, side hustlers and market traders going online for the first time.
learn: What you need on day one, and what can wait
How to choose who you sell to and say it in one line
How to test an idea before you buy stock
How to write listings and shop rules that answer questions before buyers ask
Where your first ten customers come from
biz: Shopinbos Business gives you a store at yourname.mybos.store, built with Rex from your phone. Start on the Free plan (₦0 a month, 3% per sale) and move up when you sell more.

lessons.title: What you need before you start
lessons.intro: You don’t need a shop, a laptop or a big budget. You need a phone, a few products and a way for people to pay. This lesson shows what to get ready before you open your store.
lessons.intro_pcm: You no need shop, laptop or big money. Na phone, small products and way wey people go take pay you. For this lesson, you go see wetin to arrange before you open your store.
learn: What you need on day one
How to choose your first products
steps: Start with what you already sell or can get quickly.
Your account name should match your name or business name.
Short, easy to say on a voice note, and not used by a big brand.
One clear photo of each product is enough to start.
lessons.try_pcm: Write your shop name and the first five products wey you go sell, with their price.
checks: I have a shop name
I picked my first 5 products
I know my bank account details
I have one photo of each product
lessons.quiz: What do you need most on your first day?
options: A phone, a few products and a way to get paid
lessons.why: You can start from your phone with a few products. Everything else can come later.

biz.en: Shopinbos Business builds your store from your phone. Rex asks what you sell and sets it up, and you can start on the Free plan.
biz.pcm: Shopinbos Business dey build your store from your phone. Rex go ask wetin you dey sell come set am up, and you fit start for Free plan.

lessons.try: Write down your shop name and the first five products you will sell, with their prices.

lessons.title: Choose who you sell to
lessons.intro: Trying to sell to everybody usually means nobody feels you are talking to them. When you pick one clear group of buyers, your products, prices and posts all get easier to decide.
lessons.intro_pcm: If you wan sell to everybody, nobody go feel say na dem you dey talk to. When you pick one clear group of buyers, e go easy to decide your products, price and posts.
learn: How to describe your best buyer
Where your buyers spend time online
How your buyer changes your price and words
steps: Think of your last five buyers
Or the people who ask you for things most. What do they have in common?
Age, city, job, what they earn, what they worry about. “Working mums in Abuja who have no time to go to market.”
WhatsApp groups, Instagram, TikTok, church, school, office, market.
Would this person want it, and can they afford your price?
lessons.try_pcm: Write one paragraph about your best buyer: who dem be, where dem dey stay, wetin dem need and where dem dey spend time online.
checks: I looked at my last five buyers
I described one real person
I know where they spend time online
I checked my products fit them
lessons.quiz: Which of these is a clear customer?
options: Students in Ibadan who want affordable going-out outfits
lessons.why: A clear customer tells you what to stock, what to charge and where to post.

biz.en: When you set up Shopinbos Business, tell Rex who you sell to. He uses it for your store’s words, photos and first products.
biz.pcm: When you dey set up Shopinbos Business, tell Rex who you dey sell to. E go use am for your store words, pictures and first products.

lessons.try: Write one paragraph about your best buyer: who they are, where they live, what they need and where they spend time online.

lessons.title: Describe your business in one sentence
lessons.intro: If you can’t say what you sell in one sentence, buyers won’t remember it. A clear line helps people understand you fast and tell their friends about you.
lessons.intro_pcm: If you no fit talk wetin you dey sell for one sentence, buyers no go remember am. One clear line go make people understand you quick and tell their friends about you.
learn: The three parts of a good one-liner
How to test it on real people
steps: “For working women who need office-ready outfits”.
“Delivered in Lagos within two days” or “sizes up to 22”.
Read it out. Ask them to repeat what you sell. If they can’t, make it simpler.
lessons.try_pcm: Write your one sentence, then put am for your WhatsApp bio, your Instagram bio and for the top of your store.
checks: I wrote what I sell
I said who it is for
I added one thing that makes me different
Three people understood it
lessons.quiz: Which one-liner is best?
options: The best shop in Nigeria for all your needs
Hair bundles and wigs for women in Port Harcourt, delivered in 48 hours
lessons.why: It says what you sell, who it is for and why to pick you. Fancy words say nothing.
lessons.try: Write your one sentence, then put it in your WhatsApp bio, your Instagram bio and at the top of your store.

lessons.title: Test your idea before you spend big
lessons.intro: The most expensive mistake is buying a lot of stock nobody wants. You can test demand with pre-orders, a small batch or a supplier’s stock before you put your money down.
lessons.intro_pcm: The mistake wey cost pass na to buy plenty stock wey nobody want. You fit test if people want am with pre-order, small batch or supplier stock before you put your money down.
learn: When to stop and try something else
steps: Post the product before you buy it
Use the supplier’s photo or a sample. Ask who wants it, with the price.
A deposit shows a buyer is serious. Likes and “nice” do not.
Buy 5 to 10 pieces, or dropship so you buy nothing upfront.
For example: if 5 people pay in two weeks, buy more. If not, try the next idea.
lessons.try_pcm: Pick one product idea. Post am this week with price and count how many people ask to buy or pay deposit.
checks: I picked one idea to test
I posted it with a price
I set a rule for “enough” sales
I counted real buyers, not likes
lessons.quiz: What is the strongest sign people want your product?
options: Lots of likes on your post
Buyers paying a deposit before you stock it
A friend saying it is a good idea
lessons.why: Money is the real test. Likes and compliments cost nothing.

biz.en: In Shopinbos Business you can add supplier products from Find stock and sell them without buying stock first, which makes testing cheaper.
biz.pcm: For Shopinbos Business you fit add supplier products from Find stock and sell dem without buying stock first, so to test go cheap.

lessons.try: Pick one product idea. Post it this week with a price and count how many people ask to buy or pay a deposit.

lessons.title: Write product listings that sell
lessons.intro: Five good products beat fifty rushed ones. A good listing answers the buyer’s questions so they can decide without sending you a message.
lessons.intro_pcm: Five correct products better pass fifty wey you rush. Good listing go answer buyer questions so dem fit decide without dem message you.
learn: What makes a good product title
The details buyers always ask for
How to write two lines that sell
steps: What it is, plus one detail: “Leather tote bag, brown”.
Front, back and one close-up. Show the real colour.
Say exactly what is available, and the full price.
Material, size, who it is for and how long delivery takes.
lessons.try_pcm: Rewrite the listing for your best product. Ask yourself: buyer fit order without asking me anything?
checks: My title says what it is
I have three clear photos
Sizes, colours and price are there
I wrote two helpful lines
lessons.quiz: A buyer keeps asking “what size is it?”. What should you fix?
options: Add size details to the listing
lessons.why: If people ask the same question, the answer belongs in the listing.

biz.en: In Shopinbos Business, Rex can write your product description from a photo, and each product can have sizes and colours with their own stock.
biz.pcm: For Shopinbos Business, Rex fit write your product description from picture, and each product fit get sizes and colours with their own stock.

lessons.try: Rewrite the listing for your best product. Ask yourself: could a buyer order without asking me anything?

lessons.title: Set simple shop rules: delivery, payment and returns
lessons.intro: Most arguments with buyers start because nobody agreed the rules. Write down how you deliver, how people pay and what happens if something is wrong, and show it before they buy.
lessons.intro_pcm: Most quarrel with buyers dey start because nobody agree the rules. Write how you dey deliver, how people go pay and wetin go happen if something wrong, and show am before dem buy.
learn: The three rules every shop needs
How to write them in plain words
steps: Where you deliver, how long it takes and what it costs.
How buyers can pay, and when you send the order.
What you accept, how many days buyers have and who pays delivery.
On your store, in your WhatsApp catalogue and in a saved reply.
lessons.try_pcm: Write your three rules for three short sentences each. Share am with one friend make dem tell you if anything no clear.
checks: I wrote my delivery rule
I wrote my payment rule
I wrote my returns rule
I put them where buyers can see them
lessons.quiz: A buyer says “you never told me delivery costs ₦3,000”. What would have prevented this?
options: A delivery rule shown before they ordered
lessons.why: Rules shown before the sale stop most arguments after it.

biz.en: Shopinbos Business has ready refund, privacy and delivery pages you fill in, and checkout shows your delivery fee before the buyer pays.
biz.pcm: Shopinbos Business get ready refund, privacy and delivery pages wey you go fill, and checkout dey show your delivery fee before buyer pay.

lessons.try: Write your three rules in three short sentences each. Share them with one friend and ask if anything is unclear.

lessons.title: Get your first 10 customers
lessons.intro: Your first customers almost always come from people who already know you. This lesson shows who to tell, what to say and how to turn the first few buyers into the next ten.
lessons.intro_pcm: Your first customers go mostly come from people wey don know you before. This lesson go show you who to tell, wetin to talk and how the first few buyers go bring the next ten.
learn: Why people who know you buy first
What to say when you share
How to ask happy buyers to share
What to do when the first order comes
steps: Family, friends, old classmates, colleagues, your church or mosque.
Not a broadcast. Say what you now sell and who it is for, with one photo and the price.
Post on your Status and bios
Your best product, the price and how to order.
After delivery: “If you like it, please tell one friend.”
lessons.try_pcm: Write 30 people wey you know and send personal message to ten of dem today.
checks: I listed 30 people
I sent ten personal messages
I posted on my Status
I will ask every buyer to share
lessons.quiz: Where do most first orders come from?
lessons.why: Your contacts already trust you. Start with them, then grow from there.

biz.en: Shopinbos Business gives you one store link to share everywhere, and every order lands in one list, whether it came from WhatsApp, Instagram or your store.
biz.pcm: Shopinbos Business go give you one store link wey you fit share everywhere, and every order go land for one list, whether e come from WhatsApp, Instagram or your store.

lessons.try: Write down 30 people you know and send a personal message to ten of them today.

name: Money and pricing
about: For small business owners who want to know if they are really making money. Learn your true cost per item, how to price for profit, how to price against the market, what to do when costs rise, cash flow, keeping money apart and simple bookkeeping.
for: Sellers who are busy but not sure they are making a profit.
learn: How to find your real cost per item
How to set a price that leaves profit, and margin vs markup
How to compete without a price war
How cash flow works and why busy shops run out of money
How to keep simple books in ten minutes a week
biz: Shopinbos Business shows the margin on each product, records every sale (including ones you record by hand) and pays your money out to your bank through Paystack.

lessons.title: Know your real cost per item
lessons.intro: Many sellers think their cost is what they paid the supplier. Your real cost also includes transport, packing, payment fees and the delivery you don’t charge for. Miss these and your profit disappears.
lessons.intro_pcm: Plenty sellers think say their cost na wetin dem pay supplier. Your real cost still include transport, packing, payment fee and delivery wey you no charge for. If you miss dem, your profit go disappear.
learn: How to share one cost across many items
Fixed costs vs costs per item
Why your cost changes over time
steps: Your market trip or waybill, shared across the pieces you bought.
Nylon, box, label, and the payment fee on each sale.
If you give free delivery, it is your cost.
lessons.try_pcm: Pick your best seller and calculate the real cost for each one, with every cost wey dey this lesson.
checks: I know the buying price
I shared my transport across the pieces
I added packing and payment fees
I added any delivery I cover
lessons.quiz: You bought 20 bags for ₦100,000 and paid ₦10,000 for transport. What does each bag cost you before packing?
lessons.why: ₦110,000 divided by 20 bags is ₦5,500 per bag. Transport is part of your cost.

biz.en: The free profit margin calculator does this sum for you. In Shopinbos Business, each product shows its margin once you add your cost.
biz.pcm: The free profit margin calculator go do this calculation for you. For Shopinbos Business, each product go show the margin once you add your cost.

lessons.try: Pick your best seller and work out its real cost per item, with every cost in this lesson.

lessons.title: Setting a price that leaves profit
lessons.intro: Price too low and you work for nothing. Price too high and nobody buys. Use your real costs and a margin to find the right price.
lessons.intro_pcm: If your price too low, you go dey work for nothing. If e too high, nobody go buy. Use your real cost and margin find correct price.
steps: Product, transport, packing and any delivery you cover.
Many small shops aim for 30% to 50%. Check what is normal for your product.
The payment fee (Paystack is 1.5% + ₦100, capped at ₦2,000) and any platform fee per sale.
lessons.try_pcm: Use the free selling price calculator for your top three products and compare am with your price now.
checks: I know my real costs
I picked a margin
I included payment fees
I rounded my prices
lessons.quiz: What is a 50% margin on a ₦10,000 cost?
lessons.why: Margin is profit as a share of the price. ₦10,000 profit on a ₦20,000 price is 50%.

biz.en: The selling price calculator works it out in naira. On Shopinbos Business the fee per sale is 3% on the Free plan and lower on paid plans, so include it in your price.
biz.pcm: The selling price calculator go calculate am for naira. For Shopinbos Business, the fee for each sale na 3% for Free plan and e dey lower for paid plans, so put am inside your price.

lessons.try: Use the free selling price calculator for your top three products and compare the result with your current prices.

lessons.title: Price against the market without a price war
lessons.intro: Someone will always sell cheaper. If you only compete on price, you work harder for less. You can charge a fair price when buyers can see why you are worth it.
lessons.intro_pcm: Person go always dey wey dey sell cheaper. If na only price you dey take compete, you go work hard for small money. You fit charge correct price when buyers fit see why you worth am.
learn: Why the cheapest seller often struggles
When a lower price makes sense
steps: Note their price, delivery fee and what they include.
Faster delivery, better photos, original items, a warranty, pay on delivery, kind service.
Put it in your listing and your posts, not only in your head.
“Buy 2, save ₦1,500” keeps your price strong and raises order size.
lessons.try_pcm: Compare your best seller with five other sellers. Write one reason why buyer go pay your price, and add am to your listing.
checks: I checked five other sellers
I know my edge
My edge is in my listing
I planned one bundle instead of a cut
lessons.quiz: Another seller drops their price below your cost. What is the smartest move?
options: Show why you are worth your price and offer a bundle
lessons.why: Selling below cost is a race to zero. Compete on value you can afford.
lessons.try: Compare your best seller with five other sellers. Write down one reason a buyer should pay your price, and add it to your listing.

lessons.title: When your costs go up, check your prices
lessons.intro: Supplier prices, fuel and delivery costs change often. If your price stays the same, your profit quietly shrinks. Here is how to spot it and adjust without losing buyers.
lessons.intro_pcm: Supplier price, fuel and delivery cost dey change anyhow. If your price no change, your profit go dey reduce quietly. See how to notice am and adjust without losing your buyers.
learn: Working out your profit per item
Other ways to protect your profit
steps: Product, packing and any delivery you cover.
Price minus all costs, including the payment fee.
₦500 now is easier for buyers than ₦3,000 later.
A short, honest message before the new price starts.
lessons.try_pcm: Pick your three best sellers, check how much each one dey cost you today, and see if your profit still dey where you want am.
checks: I checked today’s cost for my best sellers
I know my profit per item
I planned any price change in small steps
I will tell my regulars first
lessons.quiz: You sell a bag for ₦15,000. Your cost went from ₦9,000 to ₦10,500. How much less do you now make on each bag?
lessons.why: Every naira added to your cost comes out of your profit unless you change your price.
lessons.try: Pick your three best sellers, check what each one costs you today, and see if your profit is still where you want it.

lessons.title: Cash flow: why a busy shop can still run out of money
lessons.intro: Profit is what you make on paper. Cash flow is the money you actually have today. A shop can sell a lot and still have no money to restock, because cash is stuck in stock, debts or delayed payments.
lessons.intro_pcm: Profit na wetin you make for paper. Cash flow na the money wey dey your hand today. Shop fit sell plenty and still no get money to restock, because the cash don hook for stock, debt or payment wey never land.
learn: Planning when money comes in and goes out
steps: Sales you expect this month, and when the money will reach your bank.
Stock, rent, data, salaries, and the dates you must pay.
Stock that doesn’t move and customers who owe you are cash you can’t use.
Set aside a little from every sale until you have one month of fixed costs saved.
lessons.try_pcm: Write every payment wey you must make for the next four weeks and the money wey you expect make e enter. Mark any week where wetin dey comot pass wetin dey enter.
checks: I listed money coming in
I listed money going out
I found my tight weeks
I started a small buffer
lessons.quiz: You have ₦400,000 of stock but ₦20,000 in your account and rent is due. What is the problem?
options: Your cash is stuck in stock
lessons.why: Stock is not cash until it sells. Buy in smaller amounts and keep a buffer.

biz.en: Shopinbos Business pays your money out to your bank through Paystack, usually within a few working days. Plan your restocks around that timing.
biz.pcm: Shopinbos Business dey pay your money out to your bank through Paystack, usually within few working days. Plan your restock around that time.

lessons.try: Write down every payment you must make in the next four weeks and the money you expect in. Mark any week where out is bigger than in.

lessons.title: Keep business money and personal money apart
lessons.intro: When shop money and house money share one account, you can’t tell if you are making profit. A separate account and a simple pay-yourself rule fix that.
lessons.intro_pcm: When shop money and house money dey the same account, you no go fit know if you dey make profit. Separate account and simple rule for how you go pay yourself go solve am.
learn: What to do when you borrow from the shop
steps: Ask your bank what they need for a business account.
Make it the account your sales are paid into.
Pay yourself on a set day
A fixed amount, like ₦30,000 at the end of each month.
If you take shop money for home, note it and pay it back.
lessons.try_pcm: Decide how much you go pay yourself every month and the day wey you go do am. Write am down.
checks: My shop money has its own account
My payouts go to that account
I set my monthly pay and pay day
I write down anything I borrow from the shop
lessons.quiz: You took ₦10,000 of shop money for school fees. What should you do?
options: Write it down and pay it back
Forget it, it’s all your money
lessons.why: A simple note keeps your profit numbers honest, even when life happens.

biz.en: In Shopinbos Business, set your business account as your payout account, so every sale lands in the shop’s account, not your personal one.
biz.pcm: For Shopinbos Business, put your business account as your payout account, so every sale go land for shop account, no be your personal own.

lessons.try: Decide how much you will pay yourself each month and the day you will do it. Write it down.

lessons.title: Simple bookkeeping on your phone
lessons.intro: Bookkeeping is just writing down money in and money out. Ten minutes a week on your phone tells you what you really made.
lessons.intro_pcm: Bookkeeping na just to write money wey enter and money wey comot. Ten minutes every week for your phone go tell you wetin you really make.
steps: Including cash sales at your stall and orders from chats.
Date, what it was for and how much, in a note or spreadsheet.
Keep them in one photo album for each month.
Money in minus money out. Same day every week.
lessons.try_pcm: Start costs note today and add everything wey you spend for the shop this week, even ₦500 for nylon.
checks: I record every sale
I have a costs note on my phone
I keep my receipts in one album
I set a weekly money check
lessons.quiz: This week your sales were ₦120,000 and your costs were ₦85,000. What did you make?
lessons.why: Profit is money in minus money out: ₦120,000 minus ₦85,000 is ₦35,000.

biz.en: Shopinbos Business records every order for you, and you can record a sale made at your stall or on WhatsApp so your sales and stock stay right.
biz.pcm: Shopinbos Business dey record every order for you, and you fit record sale wey you make for your stall or for WhatsApp so your sales and stock go correct.

lessons.try: Start a costs note today and add everything you spent on the shop this week, even ₦500 for nylon.

name: Sourcing: find stock and dropship
about: For sellers deciding what to stock and where to get it. Learn dropshipping vs wholesale, how to choose products that sell, check suppliers, ask for quotes and negotiate, decide how much stock to buy and import step by step.
for: Sellers looking for products, better supplier prices or a way to sell without buying stock.
learn: When to dropship and when to buy wholesale
Four checks before you add a product
How to check a supplier before you pay
How to ask for a quote and negotiate
How much stock to buy, and how importing works

lessons.intro_pcm: For dropship, you dey sell without holding stock. For wholesale, you dey buy stock for lower price. Most shops dey use both. See how to choose.
steps: No money tied up in stock.

checks: I understand dropshipping
I understand wholesale
I compared what I keep
I picked a product to test
lessons.quiz: When should you buy a product wholesale?
options: Before you know if it sells
lessons.why: Test first. Buy stock once a product proves itself.

biz.pcm: For Shopinbos Business, Find stock go let you dropship supplier product (dem go send am to your buyer) or buy am wholesale, from one place.

lessons.title: Choosing products that sell
lessons.intro: The best products solve a need, travel well and leave you enough profit. Here is a simple test before you add anything.
lessons.intro_pcm: Better products dey solve need, dey travel well and dey leave you enough profit. See simple test before you add anything.
steps: Do people ask for it in your chats or comments?
Can you keep at least 25% after fees?
Will it arrive safe and on time?
See it with your own eyes.

checks: Buyers ask for it
I keep at least 25%
It travels well
I ordered a sample
lessons.quiz: Which product is the safest first choice?
options: A popular bag that travels well
lessons.why: Products that don’t break or spoil are easier to deliver and return.

biz.en: See which products are trending in Nigeria right now, with naira prices and where to get stock.
biz.pcm: See which products dey trend for Nigeria now now, with naira price and where to get stock.

lessons.try: Run the four checks on three products you are thinking of selling.

lessons.title: Check a supplier before you pay
lessons.intro: A bad supplier can ruin your name: late stock, wrong items or money gone. A few checks before you pay protect your money and your customers.
lessons.intro_pcm: Bad supplier fit spoil your name: stock wey late, wrong items or money wey don go. Small checks before you pay go protect your money and your customers.
learn: Why you should start with a small order
Red flags to walk away from
steps: A physical address, a registered business, and other sellers who buy from them.
Minimum order, price per piece, delivery time and what happens if items are faulty.
Order a sample or small batch
Check quality before you buy in bulk.
Prices far below everyone else, pressure to pay fast, no address, refusing a small order.
lessons.try_pcm: Pick one supplier wey you dey use or wey you wan use. Ask dem the four main questions and write their answers.
checks: I checked they are a real business
I asked about minimum order and delivery
I asked what happens with faulty items
I started with a small order
lessons.quiz: A supplier offers iPhones at half the market price, but only if you pay today. What should you do?
options: Pay fast before the deal ends
Walk away. It has two red flags
lessons.why: A price far below the market plus pressure to pay fast is a classic scam.

biz.pcm: Suppliers wey dey Find stock for Shopinbos Business don pass check, and verified badge dey show suppliers wey add their CAC registration.

lessons.title: Ask suppliers for a quote and negotiate
lessons.intro: When you want to buy more, ask suppliers for a quote. A clear request gets you a better price, faster.
lessons.intro_pcm: When you wan buy plenty, ask suppliers for quote. Clear request go give you better price quick quick.
learn: What to include in a request
steps: Ask for price per piece at two quantities
For example 20 pieces and 50 pieces, so you see the discount.
How long it takes, who pays delivery and when you pay.
Price, time and how reliable they have been. Then ask the best one to match on one point.

checks: I listed what I want
I asked for prices by quantity
I asked about delivery time
I compared two quotes
lessons.quiz: What makes a supplier reply faster with a good price?
lessons.why: Suppliers price faster when they know exactly what you need.

biz.en: In Shopinbos Business you can send a quote request to a supplier on Find stock and see their reply in one place.
biz.pcm: For Shopinbos Business you fit send quote request to supplier for Find stock and see their reply for one place.

lessons.try: Send a clear quote request to two suppliers for a product you sell often, with two quantities. Compare the replies.

lessons.title: How much stock to buy
lessons.intro: Too little stock and you miss sales. Too much and your cash is stuck on the shelf. A simple rule based on what you sell each week helps you buy the right amount.
lessons.intro_pcm: If stock small, you go miss sales. If e too much, your money go hook for shelf. Simple rule based on wetin you dey sell every week go help you buy correct amount.
learn: How to work out weekly sales
Lead time: how long restocking takes
What to do with slow stock
steps: For each product, how many sold in the last four weeks, divided by four.
How many weeks from ordering to having it in hand.
Weekly sales × lead time, plus one extra week. Reorder when stock falls to that number.
If something has not sold in 60 days, bundle it or discount it, and don’t reorder.
lessons.try_pcm: Calculate reorder point for your three best sellers and write am beside each one.
checks: I know my weekly sales
I know my lead time
I set reorder points
I listed my slow stock
lessons.quiz: You sell 5 wigs a week and restocking takes 2 weeks. When should you reorder?
